key_insight: Combining 3D welding simulations with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for reducing weld defects and stabilizing thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joints.
method: Simulate temperature, force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combine simulation and ANN predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good agreement with CEL predictions; ANN R² values ranged from 0.91 to 0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive performance outside the tested process-parameter range remains unestablished, and the abstract does not specify dataset size.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
